policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 14 May close (1x4 3.89, 3x6 4.08, 6x9 4.39, 9x12 4.64 vs WIBOR 3M 3.85) price roughly 80bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 6 May (core probably rose in April; wait-and-see); Glapiński (7 May): the probability of a hike has risen and a cut is very unlikely - a CPI breach of 3.5% with persistent forecasts would trigger action. Wnorowski (14 May): on hold at least until July, CPI above 3.5% would not trigger an automatic hike; Litwiniuk (13 May): a hike more likely than a cut. April flash CPI 3.2% (30 Apr; 3.0% expected); core 2.7% in March. The fuel VAT and excise cuts were extended to 31 May (13 May).
policy.risk_text: Glapiński (7 May) moved to hike risk: a CPI breach of 3.5% with persistent forecasts would trigger action - May CPI (29 May) and the July projection are the tests. The front end trades oil and the Iran talks; long end: heavy May supply.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after March PLN 69.6bn (25.6% of the limit); the fiscal notification and the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; the SAFE loan was signed on 8 May; fuel package (VAT 8%, minimum excise, price caps) extended to 31 May (13 May).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~51% (after 13 May, Millennium) financed; budget accounts ~PLN 184bn at end-April (MoF estimate); 8 May T-bill PLN 3.66bn at 4.151%. S&P affirmed A-/stable (8 May), DBRS A with a negative trend; Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 6 May; April CPI 3.2% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.4% y/y (flash). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable (affirmed 8 May). 14 May: Q1 GDP flash 3.4% y/y (3.6% expected), 0.5% q/q; Wnorowski: on hold at least until July, CPI above 3.5% would not trigger an automatic hike; ING: 75bp of hikes priced within 12 months, the 2Y swap at its 4.50% high (Pekao); BGK sold PLN 0.84bn of FPC bonds (demand 1.10bn) plus 0.15bn; POLGB yields fell 3-13bp on Gulf calm (DS0436 5.85%). Abroad: Trump and Xi agreed in Beijing that Hormuz must reopen but US-Iran talks stayed stalled; Brent ~$105; a 2026 Fed cut is priced out (FedWatch 28% for a hike); ~90% for a June ECB hike, almost three ECB and three BoE hikes priced; Bund ~3.05%.

calendar.plan_text: MoF May plan (30 Apr): sale auctions on 13 May (PLN 6-12bn), 21 May (7-13bn) and 27 May (6-12bn) in OK0129 (new 2Y, replaces OK0128), NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; a 46-week T-bill on 8 May (3-6bn); no switch. ~49% of 2026 needs financed after the April sales. 8 May T-bill: PLN 3.66bn at 4.151% plus 0.55bn. 13 May sale: PLN 11.01bn vs 13.73bn demand (cover 1.25) plus 0.85bn; OK0129 4.868%, PS0731 5.360%, DS0436 5.854%, PS0130 5.018%. BGK FPC (14 May): PLN 0.84bn on 1.10bn demand plus 0.15bn.
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining May sales: 21 May, 27 May. Next MPC 1-2 Jun: a hold is expected; the July projection is the next marker. Covers: 1.25 (13 May) vs 1.13-1.25 in April.

Poland's 5Y CDS was 51bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 275bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 14 May close). Trump-Xi: Hormuz must reopen; Brent ~$105 (14 May).
